reviewer: programme_learning independent agent, no native-human/educator claim
sourceClaim: Read-only scratch captures. Current canonical hashes must match before any ledger adoption. Actual question JSON contains generated evidence, not a claim that every recipe has been independently read.

referenceChecks.outcome: Treccani explicitly supports avere. No auxiliary correction.
Treccani supports avere and compete-for-post constructions.
Treccani supports no past participle/compound tenses; empty past case is unavailable, not a missing invented form.

Both auxiliary branches are supported across meanings. Live plan meaning includes achieve/obtain/follow-as-consequence, past table explicitly labels cross-construction possibilities, and doctorate context correctly accepts only ha conseguito. No definite form retirement proposed from bare table alone.
Agogniamo is the preferred transparent ending. Crusca tolerates gniamo/gnamo alternation generally; no unsupported categorical agognamo rejection proposed.
Treccani supports current assolto, and archaic verbal assoluto is distinguished from modern practical default; no automatic addition of archaic answers.
Reflexive indirect object sense and normal subject agreement supported; the separate fixed da solo scene is the exact error.

findings.reason: The shared stage/stages/staged/staging predicate describes arranging an event, not setting up a physical platform or reception centre. Exact generated output includes I stage the stage for the concert and I stage a reception centre.
findings.proposed: Use set up or source-declared per-frame English predicates. Preserve exact old selected recipes/history under the declared revision mechanism; do not alter Italian paradigms.

findings.scope: Only explicit formal feminine and plural uses of fixed frame3 la facoltà di decidere da solo; no blanket retirement of valid male singular or unlabelled io.

evidence.it: Signora Rossi, Lei si arroga la facoltà di decidere da solo.
evidence.en: Ms Rossi, you claim the authority to decide alone.

evidence.it: Signora Rossi, Lei si sta arrogando la facoltà di decidere da solo.
evidence.en: Ms Rossi, you are claiming the authority to decide alone.

evidence.it: Signora Rossi, Lei si arrogava la facoltà di decidere da solo.
evidence.en: Ms Rossi, you used to claim the authority to decide alone.

evidence.it: Signora Rossi, Lei si stava arrogando la facoltà di decidere da solo.
evidence.en: Ms Rossi, you were claiming the authority to decide alone.

findings.reason: Da solo is adjectival in this construction and agrees with the person who decides. The real mixed-transfer player says Signora Rossi ... decidere da solo. Sixteen unique explicitly feminine/plural context candidates are captured separately.
findings.proposed: Author a neutral complement or controlled gender/number frames. Retire only exact invalid old-revision recipes, retain other historical contexts and all existing event/completion history.

findings.scope: Present targets for persons0/1/2/5, including ordinary selected courtroom contexts. No proposed changes to other tenses without separate source review.
findings.reason: Treccani explicitly lists comparisco/comparisci alongside compaio/compari; the source usage already mentions comparisco. Exact gradeQuestion returns incorrect for comparisco/comparisci/comparisce/compariscono and correct for the sole accepted non-isc counterpart.
findings.proposed: Add only source-supported present alternatives to conjugator/question answer vectors while retaining the current common default and exact old question descriptor compatibility.

findings.scope: simpleExamples[1] and generated present scene1 only; its explicitly authored background counterpart already says from the crowd.

evidence.it: Me la do a gambe dalla folla.
evidence.en: I make a run for it through the crowd.

findings.reason: Dalla folla states away/from the crowd, while through the crowd changes the path and meaning.
findings.proposed: Use I make a run for it away from the crowd, preserving the exact historical selected translation under source revision handling.

findings.severity: bounded current English time/viewpoint repair candidate
findings.scope: Only background simple frame0 containing oggi. No claim that Italian imperfetto with oggi is itself invalid.

evidence.it: Io comparivo davanti al giudice oggi.
evidence.en: I used to appear before the judge today.

evidence.it: Signora Rossi, Lei compariva davanti al giudice oggi.
evidence.en: Ms Rossi, you used to appear before the judge today.

findings.reason: I used to appear before the judge today imposes habitual past on a deictic single-day cue. Italian comparivo can describe an earlier episode today; the English cue needs that viewpoint or explicit recurrent context.
findings.proposed: Author an episode translation (I was appearing...) or a recurring situation with a compatible time cue; preserve exact prior context IDs/revision.

findings.scope: Dictionary example1 only; no exact current assessed contextual question generated from its infinitive sentence in the sampled core cases.

evidence.it: Non si può condonare un abuso edilizio in area protetta.
evidence.en: An illegal building in a protected area cannot be granted an amnesty.

findings.reason: The sentence presents a timeless rule for every protected-area abuse without identifying a condono regime, date, constraint or region. The Constitutional Court describes distinct national/regional regimes and conditions; this is not a verified comprehensive current legal proposition.
findings.proposed: Use a specific fictional refusal rather than a universal legal assertion (for example, Questo abuso non è stato condonato). Do not derive a legal recommendation from this audit.

findings.scope: Usage assertion that accampare diritti means rights one is not really entitled to; selected dubious-claim scenes are coherent.

evidence.usage: Used almost only with 'scuse', 'pretesti', 'pretese' or 'diritti', and with a nuance of unjustified claim: 'accampare diritti' means to claim rights one is not really entitled to. The reflexive 'accamparsi' simply means to camp out. Regular.

findings.reason: De Mauro says especially indebitamente, and Treccani describes putting a right forward. A frequent negative implication should not become an unconditional semantic assertion.
findings.proposed: Say often with a negative or unjustified implication, while retaining the selected dubious-claim lesson sense.

findings.severity: bounded pedagogy/default candidate; not a grammar defect
findings.scope: Mandatory past case explicitly teaches learn converso and generated sono converso su una proposta comune without the rare label in those cards.

evidence.it: Io sono converso su una proposta comune.
evidence.en: I converged on a shared proposal.

evidence.it: Signora Rossi, Lei è conversa su una proposta comune?
evidence.en: Ms Rossi, did you converge on a shared proposal?

findings.reason: Treccani supports converso but explicitly says the participle and compound tenses are rare. De Mauro supports essere for this intransitive sense. No blanket rejection of those reference forms is justified.
findings.proposed: Expose rarity at the actual teaching point and consider optional/exploratory rare compound practice. Do not fabricate an unavailable form or retire valid old evidence.

findings.scope: Singular seedling background simple frames; plural habitual rooting contexts may be entirely natural.

evidence.it: La piantina attecchiva nel terreno umido.
evidence.en: The seedling used to take root in the damp soil.

evidence.it: La piantina attecchiva dopo il trapianto.
evidence.en: The seedling used to take root after transplanting.

evidence.it: La piantina attecchiva sul pendio riparato.
evidence.en: The seedling used to take root on the sheltered slope.

evidence.it: La piantina attecchiva malgrado il vento freddo.
evidence.en: The seedling used to take root despite the cold wind.

findings.reason: The same singular seedling used to take root suggests repeated rooting without supplied repeat/transplant context. Italian imperfetto also permits the ongoing establishment episode.
findings.proposed: Use was taking root for the single episode or supply explicit recurring transplant context, keeping a meaningful simple/progressive contrast.

findings.severity: bounded English editing candidates; not declared ungrammatical
findings.scope: Only staffing shortage, colleague’s choice and short-term loans frames; other frame English can stay appropriate.

evidence.it: Io colmo la carenza di personale.
evidence.en: I bridge the staffing shortage.

evidence.it: Signora Rossi, Lei colma la carenza di personale.
evidence.en: Ms Rossi, you bridge the staffing shortage.

evidence.it: Io assecondo la scelta del collega.
evidence.en: I indulge the colleague’s choice.

evidence.it: Signora Rossi, Lei asseconda la scelta del collega.
evidence.en: Ms Rossi, you indulge the colleague’s choice.

evidence.it: Io contraggo prestiti a breve termine.
evidence.en: I incur short-term loans.

evidence.it: Signora Rossi, Lei contrae prestiti a breve termine.
evidence.en: Ms Rossi, you incur short-term loans.

findings.reason: Bridge a staffing shortage / indulge a choice / incur loans are less direct learner models than fill/address the shortage / go along with a choice / take out loans. These are editing recommendations, not categorical invalid-language findings.
findings.proposed: Review per-frame English predicates for natural collocations instead of globally replacing the otherwise useful bridge/indulge/incur predicates.
